bullets.title: Warsh delivers hawkish Jackson Hole debut — September hike now near coin-flip
bullets.body: Fed Chair Warsh delivered his most hawkish remarks since taking office, stating few months of better inflation data have not convinced him that 'underlying trends have meaningfully improved' and that the Fed will 'ultimately end up hiking by early next year at the latest.' Financial conditions are 'not restrictive,' 2% PCE remains a 'firm, fixed target,' and September is now a 'close to even call.' The 2Y yield jumped 7bp while the 30Y fell 4bp, flattening the curve; the 2-10 spread collapsed to 37bps from mid-50s.

bullets.title: US macro backdrop strong despite hawkish Fed: profits +23% YoY, capex at 9% — highest since 2021
bullets.body: S&P 500 Q2 corporate profits rose 23% YoY with after-tax margins at all-time record highs; sequential profit growth was +9.1%. S&P 500 capex growing 9% YoY, the fastest since 2021, with >50% attributed to AI buildout. NY Fed Multivariate Core Trend PCE declined three consecutive months to 2.67% from 3.50% April peak, signaling gradual disinflation even as Warsh remains unconvinced.

bullets.title: Goldman flow data: defensives hit hardest since April 2025; macro products net bought on short covers
bullets.body: Goldman prime data shows L/S net leverage fell to 47.6% (1st percentile 1-year), while gross leverage rose to 207%. All defensive sectors — Health Care, Utilities, Staples — were net sold with the largest dollar net selling since April 2025; Health Care was the most net sold sector at -1.6 SDs. Single stocks net sold with short sales outpacing long buys 3.3:1, while macro products were net bought driven by short covers; ETF shorts (Small Cap, Large Cap, Tech) decreased 12% month/month.

bullets.title: Software sees largest buying day in 1 year; 8 straight days of net buying as positioning near 2020 lows
bullets.body: Yesterday was the largest net buying day for software in the past year with SaaS recording its 8th consecutive day of net buying, per MS. Software remains one of the most under-owned groups with gross/net exposure near 2020 lows. Wolfe All-SaaS index trades at 5.7x FY+2 EV/Sales but SaaS multiples contracted 2.58% week-over-week; IGV is -2.2% YTD vs S&P +12.9%.

bullets.title: Global bond yields surge to multi-year highs ahead of Warsh speech; French 30Y hits 2008 high
bullets.body: The 10-year German Bund yield hit a 15-year high, French 30-year yields rose to 4.92% (highest since 2008), and Japanese 10-year yields are pushing back toward cycle highs. USD/JPY extended gains to 159.64, the highest since August 19, as currency markets position for a more restrictive Fed.

bullets.title: Japan conducts record ¥15.4T FX intervention in one month — coordinated with US
bullets.body: Japan's Ministry of Finance spent a record $96-98.7 billion (15.4 trillion yen) over the past month to support the yen, coordinated with the US per Bloomberg. Despite the intervention, USD/JPY continues to extend gains toward 159.64, suggesting intervention is not stemming yen weakness as the rate differential widens.

bullets.title: S&P 500 making first lower high at 7,788; NVDA drove ~33% of S&P's +0.7% move while 70% of stocks declined
bullets.body: The S&P 500 made its first lower high at 7,788, increasing the probability of a meaningful reversal beyond mere consolidation, per Hedgeye. Yesterday's rally came on decelerating volume. On the day NVDA melted up, only ~30% of S&P stocks and 1 of 11 sectors closed green, highlighting extreme index concentration risk from AI names.

bullets.title: Commerce drafts rules to block Chinese access to US cloud AI chips; narrower targeting of remote access
bullets.body: The Trump administration is preparing narrower AI chip access rules targeting Chinese developers' remote access to US high-end GPUs through overseas data centers and cloud-computing workarounds, per The Information and MS. The rules aim to close key bypass points in existing hardware restrictions without a broad export ban.

bullets.title: Kalshi B200 GPU compute futures surge 12.6% to $6.25/hr; open interest up 73.5% in one day
bullets.body: September B200 GPU compute futures jumped to $6.25/hour from $5.55 the prior day (+12.6%), trading at an 18% premium to the Bloomberg spot price of $5.29/hour. The B200 pricing implies $28M/MW/Year, above Nebius' $25M/MW benchmark. Open interest hit $222.9M notional (+73.5% day-on-day), signaling acute near-term AI infrastructure capacity tightness.

bullets.title: Hedgeye August CPI nowcast: +3.50% YoY, accelerating +14bps sequentially; Middle East energy driving volatility
bullets.body: Hedgeye's August headline CPI nowcast stands at +3.50% YoY, up 2bps from the August 19 estimate and +14bps sequentially. Middle East energy market disruption is cited as the key driver of inflation volatility. European natural gas topped €70/MWh for the first time since March 19, adding to energy price pressure.

bullets.title: CXMT (Chinese DRAM) reports 873% YoY revenue growth in H1 — claims #4 global DRAM position
bullets.body: China's CXMT reported H1 2026 revenue of 150.3B yuan, up ~873% YoY from 15.44B yuan, with net income of 77.6B yuan and adjusted profit of 78.19B yuan. The company claims to be the fourth-largest DRAM maker globally. The explosive ramp poses a competitive threat to established memory players.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler CDS widening; Goldman packages synthetic swaps as NVDA CDS trades above its own cash bonds
bullets.body: Meta CDS has widened to 75–92bps and NVIDIA CDS to 54–82bps, with NVDA CDS now trading at a premium to its own cash bonds. Goldman Sachs is structuring synthetic total-return swaps on hyperscaler credit in response to the widening, a notable signal that credit markets are beginning to diverge from hyperscaler equity strength.

bullets.title: PayPal down ~17% after Advent-Stripe $50B takeover bid collapses
bullets.body: The Advent and Stripe consortium abandoned its $50 billion takeover bid for PayPal, sending PYPL shares down approximately 14-17% in pre-market trading. Options volume surged 263% above the 30-day average (161,962 contracts vs 61,572 avg) with mixed put/call sentiment (P/C 0.52).

bullets.title: BofA's Hartnett: stocks would fall >10% if Democrats take the Senate
bullets.body: Bank of America strategist Michael Hartnett warned that equity markets would decline more than 10% if Democrats gain control of the Senate. This political risk factor adds to the macro complexity of the current tape as the US election cycle approaches.

bullets.title: TrendForce: Vera Rubin ASP at 2x GB300; combined GPU production value projected at $710B next year
bullets.body: TrendForce projects Vera Rubin's average selling price will be twice that of the GB300, with the combined production value of GB300, VR200, and VR300 reaching $710 billion next year. This underpins the continued massive revenue opportunity for the AI GPU supply chain.

bullets.title: Precious metals and commodities rallying: silver +22.3% in past month, gold back above 200-DMA
bullets.body: Silver is up 1.8% today and +22.3% over the past month; gold has reclaimed its 200-day moving average with trend intact and options market flipped bullish. UBS is calling for investors to position for a commodity upcycle as global scarcity emerges as a structural theme. Oil is trading at $83.

bullets.title: US savings rate approaching historic lows; consumer spending sustainability in question
bullets.body: The US personal savings rate is nearing its lowest level in history, raising concerns about the durability of consumer spending that has supported economic growth. This coincides with C&I loan standards at the easier end of historical ranges and credit spreads for corporate bonds at historical lows.

bullets.title: PBOC boosts real estate credit support; mandates shift to completed-home sales model
bullets.body: The PBOC announced it will increase credit assistance for the real estate industry and established maximum loan limits for completed homes with up to 7-year terms. China is also pushing an orderly transition from presales to completed-home sales to reduce delivery risks, while requiring presale projects to have individual buildings topped out before sales.

bullets.title: European airline capacity moderating; Middle East capacity contracting sharply
bullets.body: UBS data shows European 4Q26 long-haul capacity growth moderating to 4.5% (vs 4.7% prior) and short-haul to 2.6% (vs 3.2% prior). Middle East capacity is contracting sharply: August -5.9% YoY, September -5.1% YoY. US domestic capacity remains depressed at -8% YoY. Southern Europe (Italy +4%, Spain +4%) is outperforming as a relative bright spot.

bullets.title: Apple raises Mac prices 21-50% despite weak demand signals; consumers holding devices longer
bullets.body: Apple raised Mac Studio prices 25-37% and Mac Mini 21-50% despite expectations for anemic ex-iPhone hardware revenue growth, suggesting demand and unit erosion ahead. 75% of US adults are indifferent to a foldable iPhone, and consumers are holding phones longer due to memory shortages limiting the upgrade cycle.
